rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Vaccination can prime or expand antigen-reactive cells without normally genetically rewriting the receptors of mature T cells.

evidence.excerpt: Vaccination generally recruits or expands existing mature receptor specificities rather than rewriting each mature receptor. Engineered TCR therapy introduces selected receptor sequences. In either case, tested recognition must still connect to naturally presenting tumour targets, useful function and healthy-tissue safety. If one beta sequence pairs with different alpha chains, a positive reconstruction of one pair does not establish the other pair's function or tumour killing.

rows.entailment: The existing receptor note explicitly distinguishes recruitment or expansion of mature specificities from introduction of engineered receptor sequences.
sourceScope: OpenStax 21.3 clonal-selection/expansion paragraphs; this is the ordinary vaccine mechanism, not an assertion about every possible intervention.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: A conventional T-cell receptor recognizes peptide with HLA; a tumour DNA alteration is an upstream antigen source, not the directly recognized object.

evidence.excerpt: A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Once the recognition mechanism is clear, a candidate source list precedes HLA matching, target selection and product construction. Confirm alteration identity, tumour specificity and biological support first. DNA, RNA and protein answer different questions, and a longer list can add uncertain calls as well as genuine candidates. A DNA alteration can nominate a possible sequence without establishing the processed peptide that a conventional T cell will recognise.

rows.entailment: The receptor paragraph defines peptide-HLA recognition, while the source paragraph makes the DNA alteration an upstream candidate. Together they prevent equating a mutation call with the recognised object.
sourceScope: OpenStax presentation paragraphs and Wells consortium methods; conventional peptide-HLA recognition is the stated scope.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Priming denotes initial activation of a naive T cell.

evidence.excerpt: Priming is a naive cell's initial activation in a supporting context. Signal one is TCR recognition of peptide-HLA, signal two includes CD80/CD86-CD28 costimulation and inhibitory context, and signal three includes differentiation-supporting cytokines. The receptor pre-exists the encounter. These signals interact over time; the model is not a three-button checklist and antigen-experienced or engineered cells can have different requirements.

sourceScope: Established activation teaching; only the definition is used, not a fresh certification of every cytokine experiment in that owner.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Dendritic-cell peptide display and supporting signals contribute to priming.

evidence.excerpt: Priming is initial activation of a naive T cell, with dendritic-cell display and supporting signals contributing. A cell translating vaccine RNA can present antigen it makes, while cross-presentation places externally acquired antigen on class I HLA. Successful priming and later tumour attack remain separate. The responding cells must reach the tumour, find an appropriate displayed target and retain useful function. These are dependencies, not a guaranteed or strictly timed chain. A shared processing defect can limit several targets; adding source sequences does not automatically remove it. Useful killing and durable benefit need their own outcome measurements.

sourceScope: OpenStax activation context and Kranz abstract; no claim that display alone is sufficient.

rows.subject: priming
rows.requirement: Direct presentation after a cell translates vaccine RNA and class-I cross-presentation of acquired antigen are distinct routes.

evidence.excerpt: Cross-presentation names a display process, whereas cross-priming names the activation of naive CD8 T cells through it, which needs supporting signals and its own readout. Direct presentation remains possible: a dendritic cell that receives vaccine messenger RNA and makes the protein itself presents it directly. A cell can also acquire already assembled peptide-HLA complexes from another cell (cross-dressing), which does not show processing by the recipient (Wakim and Bevan, Nature 2011, PMID 21455179, mouse viral infection). External antigen on class II is not cross-presentation.

evidence.excerpt: A cancer-cell fraction estimate describes the sampled cancer cells, whereas truncal describes ancestry shared across sampled branches; a subclonal alteration belongs to a subset. One small biopsy need not establish the distribution across every site. Read fraction and ancestry do not show that a peptide is displayed, and an unobserved region or insufficiently sampled alteration remains a gap rather than a demonstrated negative.

rows.entailment: The text separates a sampled cancer-cell fraction from truncal ancestry across branches and subclonal membership.
sourceScope: Carter subclonal-model context and a definition-based ancestry reading rule, not a universal clinical clonality threshold.

evidence.excerpt: In an invented comparison, candidate A has a supported tumour DNA alteration, no support in adequately assessed normal DNA and observed mutant RNA. It has progressed further as a source candidate, but processing, HLA display and T-cell recognition remain untested. Candidate B has tumour DNA support but inadequate normal coverage, so tumour specificity is still unresolved. These are evidence questions, not a numerical ranking algorithm.

sourceScope: Invented candidate premises, not a validated clinical score or an observed patient.

sourceScope: Invented evidence gap; agreement on the same reads does not create independent molecular confirmation.

rows.subject: data
rows.requirement: Fixation, alignment, contamination and uncertain junctions can generate misleading candidate calls.

evidence.excerpt: Prepared specimens and analysis can introduce misleading candidates through fixation damage, contamination, misalignment or uncertain junctions. The chosen reference transcript also matters when translating an altered sequence. Preserve specimen identity, coordinates and alleles, transcript/reference, method and software versions, usable coverage, thresholds and manual decisions so the result can be traced to its source. A filter or annotation is not independent proof of function.

rows.entailment: Fixation, contamination, misalignment and uncertain junctions are explicitly named sources of misleading candidates.
sourceScope: Wong 2014 abstract supports fixation damage; Jones methods support mapping/error/manual checks. The Wong article body was not read.
